title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1RC0LE_0RD---_0RE0RA_1LF0LB_1LA1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1RC0LE_0RD---_0RE0RA_1LF0LB_1LA1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a string of words (10)^d 0 1, read as digits d (mostly 1 to 4). The head never makes a long straight run. After step 3.3·106 it makes no run of 10 or more cells, and after step 2,791,354 it never again crosses the whole tape. It zigzags over the right part, rewriting digits as it goes. The first ~1,900 cells have not changed since step 3.3·106. Lean proves two shift rules. The rewriting rule on digits has not been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 28,954 cells have been visited and 15,412 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: e_right: E runs right over a block of 10 words. d_right: D runs right over a block of 110 words, shifting it by one cell. Both hold for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: No full sweeps, a frozen prefix
claims.text: Up to step 3·10<sup>9</sup> the last time the head reaches one end of the tape after having been at the other is step 2,791,354. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps only 24 straight runs of 10 or more cells occur, the last at step 211,281,720 (tape 14,879 cells). From step 3,401,999 on, successive snapshots agree on their first 1,850 to 2,000 cells.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: There is no sweep to speed up: the head moves in steps of a few cells, and each zigzag rewrites the digits next to it. The digit string the run leaves behind looks irregular, with no visible period. So no simple block rule describes it. The right end still grows, like the square root of the step count.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts if C reads a 1.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine does not sweep. Its head inches along in short zigzags, rewriting a string of digits written as words (10)^d 0 1. The left part of the tape stopped changing long ago, while the right part keeps changing and growing.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 28,954 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Digits written in 10s
html: Cut the tape after every 0 1: it is a string of words (10)^d 0 1 with d mostly between 1 and 4. At step 12,425,643 it begins 2 2 1 3 3 1 2 4 1 3 3 2 4 1 ....

Most machines on this list have a head that runs back and forth across the whole tape. This one does not. It last crossed the whole tape at step 2,791,354, and after step 3.3·106 it seldom moves more than a few cells in one direction. The first ~1,900 cells have not changed since then. The activity is in the right part, which still grows, roughly like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.421).
After 109 steps the tape spans 28,954 cells (61 left of the start, 23,566 right), with a density of 1s of 0.532.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A string of digit words (10)^d 0 1 with d mostly 1 to 4, rewritten by a head that moves only in short zigzags; a prefix of about 1,900 cells has frozen, and the rest keeps changing and growing.
family: zigzag rewriter of a digit string (irregular)
